title: The Erosion of Public Trust
text:
Trust is among the most fragile of social assets. Although it can take decades to build between citizens and their institutions, it can be eroded within a single scandal. Researchers studying civic life have noted that the perceived legitimacy of a government depends less on its efficiency than on the consistency of its conduct over time. When people believe that rules apply equally to everyone, their willingness to cooperate increases markedly.

Consequently, transparency has become a central concern for policymakers. Publishing budgets, disclosing conflicts of interest, and explaining decisions in plain language are measures intended to reassure the public. Critics argue, however, that disclosure alone does not guarantee accountability, since information that is published but never scrutinized may merely create an illusion of openness.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what depends less on efficiency than on the consistency of conduct?
options: The size of the civil service

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what are policymakers doing to reassure the public?
options: Publishing budgets and disclosing conflicts of interest

questions.text: What can be inferred about public trust from paragraph one?
options: It is easier to lose than to rebuild
It depends mainly on economic growth
It is unaffected by public scandals
It matters only in international relations

questions.text: What does the author imply about disclosure in paragraph two?
options: Disclosure can exist without real accountability

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being accepted as rightful or justified by the public
the quality of being open and easy to examine
the obligation to explain and take responsibility for one's actions

paragraph_translations: La confianza es uno de los activos sociales más frágiles. Aunque puede tardar décadas en construirse entre los ciudadanos y sus instituciones, puede erosionarse en un solo escándalo. Los investigadores que estudian la vida cívica han señalado que la legitimidad percibida de un gobierno depende menos de su eficiencia que de la coherencia de su conducta a lo largo del tiempo. Cuando las personas creen que las normas se aplican por igual a todos, su disposición a cooperar aumenta notablemente.

En consecuencia, la transparencia se ha convertido en una preocupación central para los responsables de las políticas públicas. Publicar los presupuestos, revelar los conflictos de intereses y explicar las decisiones en un lenguaje sencillo son medidas destinadas a tranquilizar a la población. Sin embargo, los críticos sostienen que la divulgación por sí sola no garantiza la rendición de cuentas, ya que la información que se publica pero nunca se examina puede crear simplemente una ilusión de apertura.
